jobs.description: ROLE SUMMARY Pfizer Global Supply (PGS) is putting trusted, AI-ready data at the heart of how medicines are made, tested and delivered. PGS & Enterprise Solutions Data Products & Platforms is a newly formed team with a single mission: make our data self-service and accessible, available at the right latency, and contextualized so that its meaning can be interpreted by people and by machines. Spanning Manufacturing, Quality and Supply Chain, the team owns data strategy and standards, data contextualisation and semantics, data operations, and the converged data platform estate for PGS and Enterprise Solutions – working in deep partnership with PGS business data owners, solution teams and the site network. The Director, Data Management & Engineering leads the function accountable for data quality and trust across PGS and Enterprise Solutions. The role owns the movement of data from source systems through to the point of consumption, and the assurance that what arrives is complete, accurate, traceable and fit to use. Partnering closely with PGS Data, Analytics & AI Transformation organisation and Digital solution teams, this function turns trusted, contextualised data into operating reality at scale. This role builds and runs the pipeline estate that carries it, engineers the data quality controls that hold it to account, and certifies data products as trusted. It is the operational spine of an AI-ready data foundation. The role leads a distributed team, supported by partner resources, and operates in a GxP-regulated environment where evidence of data integrity is a design requirement. What You Will Achieve Pipeline build and operations Partnering closely with PGS Data, Analytics & AI Transformation organisation and Digital solution teams, set objectives for and lead the design, build and operation of the data pipeline and integration estate connecting source systems to enterprise consumption, including manufacturing, quality, supply chain and ERP sources. Own ingestion and integration engineering from source through to MES, historian, and enterprise platforms, delivered to the architecture and integration standards set by Data Strategy & Architecture. Establish and maintain DataOps practice across the estate: release management, environment control, change and version management, and automated deployment. Own run-state performance, including monitoring, incident management, service levels and on-call arrangements, working with partner resources where the work is outsourced. Data quality and certification Lead data quality engineering across the estate: rule definition and enforcement, anomaly detection, remediation, and measurement. Own the lineage and evidence chain from source to consumption, ensuring ALCOA+ principles are demonstrably met and that data products can withstand regulatory scrutiny. Own the technical certification of data products into PGS Trusted Data, acting as an operational interface to the PGS Data, Analytics & AI Transformation organisation. Establish observability across pipelines and data products so that failures, drift and degradation are detected before consumers are affected. Regulatory and compliance Ensure all pipelines and data products meet 21 CFR Part 11, EU GMP Annex 11, GAMP 5 and applicable data integrity requirements. Maintain readiness for evolving regulatory expectations on AI, including demonstrable lineage from source to decision output. Working across the function Work with Data Platforms team on the boundary between the platform environment and the flow through it, ensuring that interface is explicit and understood by both teams. Partner with Delivery & Operations Excellence on demand shaping and sequencing, and with Domain Data Solution Leads to define and meet the measures agreed with their business counterparts. Set the direction for how the function aligns to enterprise-central capabilities — Enterprise Data Fabric (Loom), AI/ML platform, Cyber and OT Security — and represent PGS and Enterprise Solutions requirements into those forums. Leadership Build, lead and develop a distributed engineering team across multiple geographies, including recruitment, capability development and succession planning. Manage partner and contractor capacity,including the balance between colleague and contracted delivery. Represent the function with senior stakeholders across Digital, PGS and the Chief Data Officer organisation. Basic Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science or a related technical field. 8+ years of progressive experience, including 3+ years leading technical teams (7+ years with an advanced degree). Demonstrated experience owning data pipeline or integration estates at enterprise scale, including run-state accountability. Strong grounding in data quality engineering, lineage and observability practice. Experience leading distributed teams across multiple geographies and time zones. Experience managing partner or vendor delivery alongside internal teams. Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain technical positions to senior non-technical stakeholders. Proven ability to influence and align senior stakeholders across business and technology organizations. Candidate demonstrates a breadth of diverse leadership experiences and capabilities including: the ability to influence and collaborate with peers, develop and coach others, oversee and guide the work of other colleagues to achieve meaningful outcomes and create business impact. Preferred Qualifications Experience in a GxP-regulated manufacturing environment, with working knowledge of 21 CFR Part 11, EU GMP Annex 11, GAMP 5 and ALCOA+. Exposure to data product thinking, data contracts, and certification or trust frameworks. Familiarity with manufacturing and operational data sources: historians, MES, LIMS, SCADA, and ERP. Experience with modern data platform tooling, including cloud data warehousing, streaming, and orchestration. Understanding of ISA-95 and ISA-88 and their application to manufacturing data. Experience standing up or materially reshaping a function rather than inheriting a settled one. Global cultural awareness; comfort operating across time zones. Some travel expected. About the role
We're seeking an experienced software engineer to build the platform behind governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) at Anthropic. Compliance information lives across dozens of systems, from cloud infrastructure and identity providers to HR platforms and code repositories. You'll build the pipelines, integrations, and services that bring that data together and turn it into automated checks, real-time dashboards, and evidence for real time decision making, compliance obligations, and to support expanding the markets we can serve.
You will be an early member of the team, collaborating with stakeholders across Security, IT, Engineering, Privacy Engineering, Legal, Finance, and more to turn manual compliance processes into scalable, reliable systems. You will lead your own projects end to end, and you will put Claude to work as an extension of the team through agentic workflows for evidence collection, analysis, and continuous monitoring. If you've built internal platforms, data pipelines, or privacy systems, you'll feel right at home, and you don't need a compliance background to get started.

Design and build data pipelines that aggregate risk, control, and asset information from across Anthropic's technology stack, solving hard integration problems like disparate schemas, inconsistent data quality, and unified views of posture
Build and maintain integrations connecting our platform to cloud infrastructure, identity management, HRIS, ticketing, version control, and CI/CD systems to enable automated evidence collection and continuous validation
Translate written policies and regulatory requirements into policy-as-code, turning static documents and spreadsheets into enforceable rules, automated checks, and continuous monitoring
Design and deploy agentic workflows where Claude handles work that previously required manual effort, such as analyzing evidence, generating audit responses, and monitoring control effectiveness
Develop dashboards and reporting that provide real-time visibility into risk and compliance posture for audiences ranging from engineers to executives and external auditors
Make architectural decisions that shape how the platform grows, establishing patterns and tooling that other engineers will build on

Proven track record delivering systems supporting multi-platform deployments - from desktop clients to mobile phone clients to console clients - including the bandwidth, storage, and memory realities each platform imposes.
Experience building systems in resource-constrained environments where every CPU cycle and byte counts.
A background in game engine development, game networking, asset pipelines, or content streaming, with deep familiarity in game loop architecture, state synchronization, and how assets are loaded, prioritized, and made available to the running experience. Preferred)

jobs.description:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge.
Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. This organization is for individuals who appreciate challenging themselves and thrive on curiosity.
We operate with a flat organizational structure. All employees are expected to be hands-on and to contribute directly to the company’s mission. Leadership is given to those who show initiative and consistently deliver excellence. Work ethic and strong prioritization skills are important.
All employees are expected to have strong communication skills. They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates.
ABOUT THE ROLE:
We are looking for a Manager of Engineering to own the design, build-out, commissioning, and continuous improvement of automation, controls, and electrical systems at SpaceX’s power generation facility in Southaven. This plant is critical infrastructure for SpaceX’s AI supercomputers: it must deliver high-reliability power and supporting utilities at scale, with the uptime and response expected of a mission-critical compute campus.
If it has a gas or steam turbine control system, a switchgear lineup, a plant electrical distribution network, a SCADA/DCS point, a control loop, or a supporting utility/process system (water, wastewater, fuel gas, HVAC, cooling) that must run reliably, this team designs it, specifies it, commissions it, and keeps it running. As a Manager, you will lead a team of engineers in a high-reliability, fast-paced environment. This is a hands-on technical leadership role — you will review P&IDs, challenge control philosophies, dive into DCS/PLC architecture, electrical protection schemes, and commissioning details, not just manage a roadmap. You will scale both the team and the systems as generation capacity and AI compute load grow.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Own automation, controls, and electrical scope for power generation assets (gas turbine simple cycle, combined cycle, and steam turbine systems) and plant electrical systems, including DCS/SCADA architecture, PLC systems, turbine control interfaces, switchgear, protection and metering, plant distribution, instrumentation, and control networks — from control philosophy through commissioning and reliability, in compliance with NFPA 70/70B/70E, NESC, and IEEE standards.
Lead controls scope for mechanical and electrical balance-of-plant and supporting utilities, including fuel gas, HVAC, fire protection, compressed air, cooling water, raw water intake, demineralization, wastewater treatment, and industrial gas systems that keep the plant and downstream compute campus online.
Build, mentor, and manage a team of automation and controls engineers and technicians; scale the team with power generation capacity growth and AI supercomputer demand.
Review and approve control philosophy documents, I/O lists, control narratives, single-line diagrams, electrical/pneumatic schematics, cause-and-effect diagrams, and control panel designs; drive standardized DCS/PLC/SCADA architecture, cybersecurity posture, documentation, and engineering practices across the Southaven facilities.
Interface with internal engineering, construction, OEMs (turbine, HRSG, BOP, and electrical equipment vendors), and contractors; develop SOWs, negotiate, and manage contractor work to keep controls and electrical scope integrated and on schedule.
Own field commissioning for automation, controls, and electrical systems (loop checks, functional testing, protection testing, start-up, and hand-off) and drive root-cause investigations and reliability improvements on operating assets.
BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:
Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, Automation Engineering, or related engineering field.
8+ years of experience in automation and controls engineering, with direct experience on industrial power generation projects (gas turbine, combined cycle, or steam systems preferred) or large-scale critical power infrastructure.
3+ years of experience directly managing or leading a team of engineers (and preferably technicians).
PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCES:
Hands-on experience with DCS, PLC, HMI, and SCADA platforms used in power generation or heavy industry (e.g., Emerson, ABB, Siemens, Allen-Bradley, SEL, Ignition), including IEC 61131 programming, industrial networking (IT/OT), and protocols such as Modbus and DNP3.
Direct experience with gas turbine or combined-cycle plant controls (turbine control systems, HRSG controls, plant-wide DCS integration, and BOP), plus water treatment, wastewater, fuel gas, or process cooling systems supporting generation.
Working knowledge of utility-scale and low-voltage electrical power systems, switchgear, protection, metering, and their interface with automation and controls.
Experience designing or reviewing industrial control panels and electrical schematics (NFPA 79 / UL 508A; EPLAN, AutoCAD Electrical, or similar) across the full project lifecycle: design, procurement, construction support, commissioning, and operations.
Experience managing EPC and OEM interfaces on multi-discipline power or capital projects, and scaling a controls engineering function in a fast-growing organization.
PE license in Electrical or Controls Engineering (or willingness to pursue); familiarity with ICS cybersecurity frameworks (e.g., NERC CIP); experience supporting high-availability generation for critical or data center loads.
Excellent communication skills with the ability to remain deeply technical while mentoring engineers.
ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
Willingness to perform hands-on work in all environments (heat, cold, rain), in tight quarters or at heights, while remaining focused in hazardous environments and wearing appropriate PPE; ability to lift up to 25 lbs unassisted.
Ability to work extended hours and weekends as needed, and to provide 24/7 on-call support for emergencies, to support power generation and critical compute operations.
Must be able to work on-site at the Southaven power generation facility, with potential travel to other SpaceX sites.
